newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament seals banking guarantee law.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament seals banking guarantee law.

text.p: Polish legislators on Thursday gave final approval to a bill strengthening the banking guarantee fund (BFG) and increasing its protection of individual savers' deposits.

In a series of votes, the lower house of parliament approved several senate amendments to the bill, the most important of which raised premiums paid to the fund by the banks to give more solid funding.

The bill, which now needs to be signed by President Aleksander Kwasniewski to become law, provides for increased guarantees for individual savers' deposits from the current 3,000 Ecus to the equivalent of 4,000 Ecus, as off August this year, and to 5,000 Ecus from the begining of 1998.
The draft law would also give the fund access to more information on ailing banks and enforce better cooperation among the fund and administrators of bankrupt banks.
The fund was created in 1995 to take over guarantees of bank deposits from the state treasury and to help ailing banks restore financial liquidity.
